title: Send a pull-back toy car through a gate: press it down, drag it back to wind it, and let go cleanly
instruction: Wind up the toy car by pressing it onto the mat and pulling it backwards, then let it go behind the blue start line so that it drives itself through the wooden gate to the foam block. Do not push, throw or carry it past the line.
context: Pull-back cars are in almost every toy box, and winding one up and letting it race is play every child and parent knows. The motor inside winds only while the rear wheels roll backwards on the floor, so the car has to be held down firmly while it is dragged back: held lightly, its tyres skid and it hardly winds. Then the hand must let go cleanly, with the car still and pointing straight at the gate: it sets off the moment it is free and cannot be steered, and the gate is 120 mm wide for a 54 mm car about 40 cm away, so a few degrees of error at the release misses it. Pressing a part onto a surface while dragging it, then an aimed, clean release of something that moves by itself, is ordinary for people and rare among robot tasks.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases (bases 610 apart): x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. 1) Mat: a Fiskars self-healing cutting mat, 24 x 36 in (610 x 914, 1.5 thick, grey), its centre at x 383, y 40, long side along y, taped to the table. 2) Car: a KiNSMART 2017 Ford GT 1:38 die-cast pull-back car (part KT5391, about 7 USD; listing: 127 long, 57 wide, 32 tall, 109 g), rubber tyres. At the start it stands on the mat with the middle of its wheelbase at x 225, y -285, nose turned 20 degrees off the lane toward +x (pointing 70 degrees from +x). 3) Start line: a 24 mm strip of blue painter's tape across the mat, its near edge at y -200. 4) Gate: two wooden unit blocks (35 x 70 x 140, the standard unit block) standing on end, taped down, their 70 sides across the lane, inner faces at x 150 and x 270 (120 apart), centred on y 120. 5) Backstop: a Gaiam EVA foam yoga block (9 x 6 x 4 in, 229 x 152 x 102) lying flat, its long side across the lane, centred on x 210, near face at y 320. The lane is the line x 210; the bay is the mat between the gate and the backstop. The left arm has no job and stays in its ready pose.
scoring: Judged from the overhead trial video and a tape measure; the first rule that applies. 0: the car is not let go standing on the mat with its nose short of the start line's near edge, still (under 2 mm of motion between video frames at 30 frames/s as the fingers come off), after being pressed and drawn back on its wheels at least 2 cm in the hand's last hold; or a hand touches it again after the release; or it does not then move forward by itself at least 1 cm (it was not wound). Doing nothing scores 0, and so does a car pushed, thrown or carried past the line. 1.0: after the release it drives by itself between the posts without touching either and comes to rest upright in the bay. 0.75: it passes between the posts but brushes one, or does not come to rest upright in the bay. 0.5: it drives itself at least 30 cm forward but misses the gate. 0.25: it moves forward by itself but less than 30 cm.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 seconds at 20 steps per second)
reset_notes: About 20 seconds. Nothing is used up. Lift the car (lifting lets its wheels spin and the spring unwind), set it on its start mark (a pencil outline on the mat) turned 20 degrees off the lane, and return both arms to the ready pose. Check the gate is 120 mm wide with a ruler and the blocks are still taped down. Before each set of trials (pull-back motors vary from unit to unit): press the car onto a hard floor, pull it back 7.6 cm (3 in) and let go; it must run 2 to 3.5 m and veer less than 5 cm in 1 m, otherwise use another car. The kit costs about 90 USD: car 7, mat 64, yoga block 13, two unit blocks and tape.
fidelity: True-size car, mat, posts and backstop built from boxes and cylinders. The motor is modelled, not the gears: rear tyres rolling back wind it (2.4 N at the tyres, clutch slips after 10 cm); let go, it drives through a 15:1 slower train and frees itself when unwound. 7.6 cm of pull gives about 2.5 m on a hard floor, inside 8-12 ft quoted for a few inches; motor, friction and sizes are estimates. No speed is written to the car. Contacts are judged by geometry.
